paragraphs: Paul resolved in the Spirit to head for Jerusalem and then Rome (Acts 19:21), but a riot got to Ephesus first. Listen to how Demetrius pitches it. The shrine business is "our source of prosperity" (Acts 19:25), and Paul says "man-made gods are no gods at all" (Acts 19:26). Friend, when the truth lands on somebody's paycheck, it gets LOUD, so don't be shocked when it happens to you.

Now look at the crowd. The text says "most of them did not even know why they were there" (Acts 19:32), and they still shouted for about two hours (Acts 19:34). I've seen this before. It's like jumping into a group chat of forty people and typing the loudest thing without reading one message. Know WHY you're standing where you stand, baker, because a loud voice is not the same as a good reason.

Then the city clerk says something worth noticing. He tells the crowd the men they dragged in have "neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess" (Acts 19:37). That's what I want said about me when things get loud: nothing sticks, because I did nothing to make it stick. Live honest, stay steady in the Word, and hang on to your apron, because this story isn't over.
